title: Agent Spending Policy
description: A vendor-neutral description of what an AI agent is allowed to spend, on whom, and when a human must approve it. This is a draft (v0.1) reference format, not a standard and not an implementation of any product. See MAPPING.md for how each field relates to specific payment providers' native settings.

agent_id.description: Opaque identifier for the agent this policy applies to, scoped by whatever system issues it.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. USD, EUR) or a short uppercase asset ticker (e.g. USDC) that all amount fields in this policy are denominated in.

per_transaction_cap.description: Maximum amount allowed for a single transaction, expressed as an integer in minor units of `currency` (e.g. cents for USD, the smallest whole unit for the named asset).

window_caps.description: Rolling-window spending caps. At most one entry per `period`.

period.description: The rolling window this cap applies to.

amount.description: Maximum total spend allowed within the window, in minor units of `currency`.

merchant_allowlist.description: Exact merchant or recipient identifiers (hostname, wallet address, or provider-assigned merchant ID) this agent may pay. If present and non-empty, only these are permitted.

merchant_denylist.description: Merchant or recipient identifiers this agent may never pay, checked regardless of the allowlist.

category_allowlist.description: Optional: merchant category codes (MCC) or provider-defined category labels this agent may pay into. If present and non-empty, only these are permitted.

category_denylist.description: Optional: merchant category codes (MCC) or provider-defined category labels this agent may never pay into.

approval_threshold.description: Amount at or above which a payment must be routed to a human instead of executing automatically.

amount.description: Amount at or above which human approval is required, in minor units of `currency`.

channel.description: Opaque reference to where the approval request is routed (e.g. an email address, a Slack channel, a ticket queue ID). This schema does not define channel formats or delivery.

valid_until.description: RFC 3339 timestamp after which this policy is no longer valid and must be treated as expired.

idempotency_required.description: If true, the enforcing system must reject a retried payment request that reuses an idempotency key already recorded for this agent.

^x-.description: Vendor- or deployment-specific extension field. Consumers that don't recognize an x- field must ignore it, not reject the policy.
